reports.title: Main Estimates / Budget principal 2026–2027
reports.publisher: Department of Finance and Treasury Board, Province of New Brunswick
reports.description: The province's annual Main Estimates presenting the financial plan of estimated revenues and expenditures for the fiscal year ending 31 March 2027, including ordinary, capital and special-purpose accounts and the comparative statement of estimated revenue by source.

reports.title: Estimates of Revenue and Expenditures 2026-2027
reports.publisher: Department of Finance and Affordability, Government of Prince Edward Island
reports.description: The operating budget estimates of revenue and expenditure detailing the province's spending plans by department for the fiscal year commencing 1 April 2026.

reports.title: Estimates of the Program Expenditure and Revenue of the Consolidated Revenue Fund 2026-27
reports.publisher: Department of Finance, Government of Newfoundland and Labrador
reports.description: The annual Estimates presenting program expenditure and revenue of the Consolidated Revenue Fund for the fiscal year 2026-27, tabled as supplementary information to the Budget Address.

reports.title: Budget 2026-27: Defending Nova Scotia
reports.publisher: Department of Finance and Treasury Board, Government of Nova Scotia
reports.description: The province's annual budget documents including the Budget Address, Estimates and Supplementary Detail, Highlights, Government Business Plan and four-year fiscal projections for the 2026-27 fiscal year.

reports.title: 2026/27 Budget and Business Plan
reports.description: The annual municipal operating budget ($1.45 billion) and capital budget ($316.7 million) approved by Regional Council, setting tax rates and funding municipal services for the fiscal year.

reports.title: Property Assessment Roll and Notices (Property Valuation Services Corporation)
reports.description: Annual delivery of the Assessment Roll to Nova Scotia's 49 municipalities and Property Assessment Notices to property owners, used by municipalities to set property tax rates under the Assessment Act.

reports.title: Property Assessments (Municipal Assessment Agency)
reports.description: Annual real property assessments provided to over 230 municipalities (excluding the City of St. John's) under the Assessment Act, 2006, forming the basis for municipal property tax levies.

reports.title: Property Assessment Notices and Roll (Service New Brunswick Property Assessment)
reports.description: Annual real property assessments at market value for all properties in New Brunswick under the Assessment Act, delivered as Property Assessment Notices and used by the province and local governments to set property tax rates and levies.

reports.title: 2026 Budget Paper on the Economy
reports.publisher: Department of Finance and Affordability, Government of Prince Edward Island
reports.description: Supporting economic outlook document published with the 2026-27 operating budget, providing the growth, inflation and other assumptions underlying the fiscal forecasts.

reports.title: Property Assessment Notices and Assessment Roll (Taxation and Property Records)
reports.publisher: Taxation and Property Records, Department of Finance and Affordability, Government of Prince Edward Island
reports.description: Annual determination of market value for all real property under the Real Property Assessment Act, forming the basis for provincial and municipal property tax collection; Notices of Property Assessment are issued with the annual property tax bill.

reports.title: Municipal Assessment Agency Annual Report
reports.description: Annual performance and financial report of the Municipal Assessment Agency, including assessed property values used by municipalities to calculate tax revenue for the following year.

reports.title: City of Fredericton Consolidated Financial Statements
reports.description: Audited consolidated financial statements of the City of Fredericton for the year ended 31 December, including property tax revenue and community funding/equalization grant lines.

reports.title: City of St. John's Budget 2026
reports.description: Annual municipal operating and capital budget setting mill rates and funding municipal services, with residential and commercial realty tax revenue based on assessed values.

reports.title: Property Valuation Services Corporation Annual Report
reports.description: Annual report of the independent assessment authority, including audited financial statements, Assessment Roll quality measures, and delivery of the roll to the 49 municipalities.

dependencies.basis: The Main Estimates list Fiscal Equalization Payments as a distinct unconditional grant revenue line under Unconditional Grants – Canada, with the 2026–2027 estimate of $3,360,010 thousand dollars explicitly recorded as the amount receivable from the federal Equalization program. The document states: "Fiscal Equalization Payments / Paiements de péréquation fiscale 3,360,010"

The Main Estimates record the Canada Health Transfer as a distinct unconditional grant revenue line under Unconditional Grants – Canada for the 2026–2027 fiscal year. The document states: "Canada Health Transfer / Transfert canadien en matière de santé 1,203,400"

The Main Estimates record the Canada Social Transfer as a distinct unconditional grant revenue line under Unconditional Grants – Canada for the 2026–2027 fiscal year. The document states: "Canada Social Transfer / Transfert canadien en matière de programmes sociaux 376,000"

The 2026-2027 Estimates of Revenue and Expenditures explicitly list Equalization as a line under Revenue from Government of Canada, with the Budget Estimate of $722,707,000 for the fiscal year commencing 1 April 2026. The document states: "Equalization…………………………………………………………………… 722,707,000"
The Estimates list Canada Health Transfer as a distinct federal revenue line for 2026-2027. The document states: "Canada Health Transfer…………………………………………………………………………….. 253,531,000"
The Estimates list Canada Social Transfer as a distinct federal revenue line for 2026-2027. The document states: "Canada Social Transfer……………………………………………………………………………… 79,207,000"

The Budget 2026-27 revenue outlook states Nova Scotia’s Equalization entitlement estimate for 2026–27 is $3.5 billion and records Equalization Payments under Ordinary Revenue – Federal Sources; the program grows with the three-year average of national nominal GDP. The document states: "Nova Scotia’s entitlement estimate for 2026–27 is $3.5 billion, an increase of $73.6 million or 2.1 per cent compared to the 2025–26 Budget Estimates... The Equalization program is legislated to grow by the three-year average growth rate of national nominal Gross Domestic Product (GDP). For 2026–27 the growth rate is 3.79 per cent and the national funding pool for distribution is $27.2 billion."
Budget 2026-27 records the Canada Health Transfer under Ordinary Revenue – Federal Sources with the 2026-27 estimate of $1,507,399 thousand. The document states: "Canada Health Transfer 1,507,399"
Budget 2026-27 records the Canada Social Transfer under Ordinary Revenue – Federal Sources with the 2026-27 estimate of $470,934 thousand. The document states: "Canada Social Transfer 470,934"

The Statements and Schedules 2026 accompanying the Estimates list Equalization as a distinct Government of Canada revenue component for 2026-27 (approximately $182 million). The document states: "Equalization 2% 181,888"

Property tax revenue in the City of Fredericton financial statements is calculated from assessed values provided by Service New Brunswick Property Assessment under the Assessment Act. The document states: "Property taxes 156,346,042"

The Annual Report reports on the delivery and quality of the Assessment Roll that is the primary product of PVSC. The document states: "Each December, we deliver an Assessment Roll to all 49 Nova Scotia municipalities"
